bullets.title: MRVL: Beat/raise impresses but trades off 8% on high bar; October Analyst Day is next catalyst
bullets.body: Marvell Q2 FY27 revenue $2.74B (+37% YoY) and EPS $0.94 beat consensus, with FY27 total rev guidance raised to ~$12B (+45% YoY) and FY28 to ~$18B (+50% YoY). Data center expected +60% FY27 and >60% FY28; Google warrant deal adds potential $10B+ custom revenue in FY29+. Stock dropped 8% pre-market despite bulls citing sell-side 86% Buy consensus and avg PT $286.85 (18.8% upside); key debate is whether Google deal upside is already priced into FY28. October Analyst Day flagged as re-rating catalyst. PT range: Roth $350, KeyBanc $400, Opco $350, Citi $275, UBS $310, Wolfe $280, Oppenheimer $325.

bullets.title: NVDA: Record Q2 $96B revenue (+106% YoY); Q3 guided $108B; stock +8%, biggest one-day market cap gain ever
bullets.body: Nvidia posted its 16th consecutive revenue beat with Q2 revenue of $96B (+106% YoY) and net income of $59.7B (+126% YoY) at a 66% margin, then guided Q3 to ~$108B (+89% YoY). The print added ~$500B in market cap on the day (Trump publicly congratulated Jensen) and drove NASDAQ +1.56%. Key watch: NVDA pausing some AI cloud revenue-sharing deals (later denied by company) and acquiring Hugging Face for $12.9B. HSBC raised PT to $365 from $360; Tom Lee sees NVDA as still inexpensive; Hedgeye flagged $218 breakout with buy range $207-$230.

bullets.title: RBRK: Strong F2Q beat on NNARR acceleration to 35% YoY; FY27 ARR guidance raised; PT range $109-$125
bullets.body: Rubrik F2Q27 subscription ARR of $1,661M (+32.5% YoY) beat consensus; NNARR of $96M accelerated to 35% YoY vs 16% in prior quarter. Operating income of $33M dramatically beat the -$5M consensus. FY27 ARR guidance raised to $1.88-1.885B (+29% YoY), revenue to $1.685-1.693B (+28% YoY), and FCF margin guided 19.4%. Stock declined 7% AH on Cloud NNARR migration comp headwinds. Sell-side bulls: Wolfe PT $120 (Outperform), KeyBanc PT $120, GS PT $120, Roth PT $125, BTIG PT $125, Mizuho PT $112 (all Buy/OP); Citi more cautious at $96 with downside risk from 2H Cloud NNARR deceleration.

bullets.title: AFRM: +13% on blowout FQ4; GMV +36% YoY, Affirm Card GMV +124%; FY27 guidance ahead of Street
bullets.body: Affirm Q4 revenue $1.166B beat $1.11B estimate; GMV grew 36% YoY to $14.1B vs 29% expected; GAAP margins 12.6% vs 11% expected. Affirm Card GMV surged 124% YoY to $2.8B (20% of company GMV), active consumers +21% to 27.8M, active merchants +51%. UBS raises PT to $90 (from $82) on 29x CY28 EPS. Citi raises estimates; Jefferies bullish on FY27 expansion. Positive read-throughs flagged for V/MA and consumer finance peers COF/SYF.

bullets.title: RBRK (separate from MRVL): Rubrik beats all metrics; raised FY27 ARR/revenue/FCF guidance
bullets.body: Rubrik F2Q27 subscription NNARR accelerated to ~35% YoY (highest since F4Q25). Revenue $427M (+38% YoY) beat Street at $396M; operating margin ~8% vs Street -2%. FY27E ARR guide raised to $1.880-1.885B, revenue to $1.685-1.693B, FCF margin guided to 19.4%. No deals pulled forward; cloud migration tailwind has abated. GS raised PT to $120 from $106.

bullets.title: CIEN: JPM previews F3Q26 beat/raise; OW with $635 PT after 35% YTD drawdown
bullets.body: JPMorgan expects Ciena to report F3Q26 revenue of $1.67B (vs $1.64B consensus) and EPS $1.76 (vs $1.73) when it reports Sept 3. Orders expected to reaccelerate; component cost inflation concerns easing. Stock is down 35% since last earnings and now trades ~20x CY28E EPS. Operating margins expected to reach ~35% by end of forecast period with $20 CY28 EPS target. PT $635 (Dec-27) at 32x CY28 EPS.

bullets.title: CRDO: JPM OW, $335 PT; expects beat-and-raise F1Q27 on Optical ramp and SpaceX upside
bullets.body: Credo down >20% from June peak provides attractive entry per JPMorgan, which forecasts F1Q27 revenue of $490M (above $465-475M guidance and $473M consensus) and EPS of $1.23 vs $1.16 consensus. FY27 revenue forecast of $2.54B (+90% YoY) driven by AEC growth and Optical ZeroFlap Optics ramp to $700M+ in 2H FY27. SpaceX opportunity estimated at ~$300M in CY25. Reports Sept 1.

bullets.title: APP: Wolfe initiates at Outperform, PT $415 (33% upside) on 30%+ revenue growth trajectory
bullets.body: Wolfe initiates AppLovin at Outperform with $415 PT based on 16x FY27 EBITDA. APP maintains best-in-class ~80% EBITDA margins, highest ROAS in industry, and e-commerce vertical at $1B+ run rate with improving ROAS as it scales. FY27E revenue estimate $10.3B. Stock trading at 12.1x FY27 EBITDA after 50% YTD decline. Premarket +1.0%.

bullets.title: META: $18B settlement with 48 states over addictive design; product changes could impact engagement
bullets.body: Meta settled a federal lawsuit with 48 U.S. states for ~$18B over 10 years regarding addictive design and child data collection, a fraction of the $1.4T potential penalty. Settlement requires tighter parental controls and usage limits but does not affect thousands of other pending cases. Hedgeye flagged META as bearish (sell range $531-$586). Separately, one desk added to META short via FBY on rally.

bullets.title: GOOGL: EU search ranking changes +0.3% premarket; FTC in final stages of YouTube lawsuit prep
bullets.body: Google is changing how third-party content ranks in European search to appease antitrust regulators, gaining +0.3% in premarket. Separately, FTC is in final stages of preparing a potential lawsuit against YouTube over consumer-protection law violations related to user account suspensions. Hedgeye has GOOGL in bearish sell range $336-$348.

bullets.title: EQIX/DLR: MS reiterates EQIX as Top Pick; data centers preferred over towers on compute supply/demand
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley analysis shows EQIX and AMT are most under-owned by top 100 active managers at 4bps vs S&P 500 weight. MS reiterates EQIX as Top Pick on strong network effects and ~13% revenue growth path to 2029. Prefers data center operators over towers given favorable compute supply/demand dynamics; towers trade near trough multiples with SpaceX uncertainty overhang. DLR represents 0.08% of portfolios.

bullets.title: SNDK: Breaks bearish trend; $31B Japan NAND investment with Kioxia planned through 2032
bullets.body: Hedgeye's risk range signal changed SNDK from Bullish to Bearish trend. Separately, SanDisk and Kioxia committed $31B+ in Japan manufacturing investments through 2032 (first phase ¥1.8T new fab in northern Japan) to compete with YMTC. SK Hynix CEO projects global memory shortage to persist through end of 2030. Premarket SNDK -2.3%.

bullets.title: IREN: FY26 adj EBITDA $19.2M misses $34.9M est; $684M net loss on $450M non-cash impairments from mining conversion
bullets.body: Iris Energy reported Q4 revenue $137M (slight beat vs $135M) but adj EBITDA of $19.2M missed estimates of $34.9M by a wide margin. The $684M net loss was primarily driven by $450M non-cash impairments from decommissioning mining hardware for AI conversion. Stock down 5.7% premarket. Twitter commentary mixed: CIFR cited as better risk/reward ($7B vs IREN's $14.5B market cap despite comparable backlogs).

bullets.title: CRM: +22.5% on day; SaaS sentiment shifting from 'SaaSpocalypse' to 'SaaS Renaissance'
bullets.body: Salesforce surged 22.5% on the day, its best earnings move in ~6 years, with first cRPO beat in 3 quarters (14% vs 13%). The print alongside CRWD +20.5%, OKTA +28%, and PANW +12.8% helped IGV software ETF rise 7.7% on the day (+47% from April lows, at YTD highs). The absence of meaningful competitive threats from frontier AI vendors is helping SaaS sentiment inflect. JPMorgan notes software L/S ratio at 4th percentile since 2018.

bullets.title: DELL/AVGO/MDB/HPE/CIEN scheduled to report next week; consensus estimates provided
bullets.body: Upcoming earnings calendar: DELL reports Tue Sept 1 after close (EPS est $4.91, rev $44.93B); MDB Tue Sept 1 after close (EPS $1.62, rev $735M); AVGO Wed Sept 2 after close (EPS $3.22, rev $29.24B); HPE Wed Sept 2 after close (EPS $0.93, rev $11.95B); CIEN Thu Sept 3 before open (EPS $1.73, rev $1.64B). AI capex read-throughs from NVDA beat expected to set favorable bar.

bullets.title: ADSK: Beat/raise but -4.7% premarket on elevated expectations; UBS raises PT to $325
bullets.body: Autodesk F2Q27 revenue $2.05B (+14% CC) beat consensus by $33M; EPS $3.30 beat by $0.18; FY27 organic billings guidance raised to 9-10% from 8-9%; operating margin 41% vs Street 39.4%. Stock weak due to high bar (up ~30% past month), MaintainX dilution noise, and FY28 growth debate. UBS raises PT to $325 (Buy), Wolfe OW $350, Mizuho OP $375, KeyBanc OW (PT $215 to $215 raised).

bullets.title: GEV: New CFO Claire McDonough named, effective Jan 1, 2027; Ken Parks retiring
bullets.body: GE Vernova appointed Claire McDonough as CFO effective January 1, 2027, replacing Ken Parks who is retiring. No change to business outlook or guidance communicated alongside the announcement.

bullets.title: Jackson Hole / Warsh: Macro investors await policy signal; 54% expect risk-on reaction, 37.5% expect hawkish tone
bullets.body: Fed Chair Warsh's 10am ET speech at Jackson Hole is the key macro event. Survey data: 54% of investors expect risk-on reaction, 37.5% neutral, 4% risk-off; 37.5% expect hawkish, 37.5% neutral, 25% dovish; 65% expect process-heavy speech without fresh signals (viewed as dovish dodge). JPM notes tactically bullish but lower conviction—if both NVDA and Warsh disappoint, 3-4% SPX pullback risk. Anchored 10yr yields (current 4.60-4.76% risk range) would be market positive for EPS momentum and GARP factors.

bullets.title: NVDA revenue-sharing pause: company initially paused then denied; circular financing risk flagged
bullets.body: Reuters and WSJ reported Nvidia paused some revenue-sharing deals with AI cloud companies (SharonAI, Firmus) announced in July. Nvidia later denied the pause, saying the new model 'opens up compute access to fast-growing segments.' Bear case: rising GPU rental prices may be unsustainable if NVDA exits the rental market; $800B in total AI supply chain guarantees per BIS. Hedgeye 'snake oil' piece flagged $105B OpenAI guarantee. Antitrust concerns cited as reason for potential model revamp.

bullets.title: Chip tariff risk emerging; Trump admin weighing sweeping tariffs on semis, laptops, DC servers
bullets.body: Jefferies flagged that the Trump administration is weighing sweeping tariffs on semiconductors, laptops, gaming consoles, and data center servers—a potential headwind for the entire AI hardware supply chain. No formal announcement has been made; monitoring required ahead of any policy action. Broader semi sector down premarket: INTC -2.2%, COHR -2.2%, CRDO -2.0%, NBIS -2.1%, AXTI -2.6%, AAOI -2.4%.
